messages.message:
Patch Set 2:

(1 comment)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see the inline comment.

The leftover mounts come from test_180(), test_311() and test_312(): they call setupall() but only reach cleanupall() on the success path, so any error() in between leaks the mount into the next subtest. Adding `stack_trap 'cleanupall' EXIT` right after setupall() in those three would clean up where the leak actually happens, and would let reinit_dlc() keep failing hard on unconfigure errors that are not caused by a leftover mount. As written, every `lnet unconfigure` failure is silently recovered from, including the LNet reference leaks sanity-lnet exists to catch.

Uploaded patch set 3.

commit.subject: LU-20619 tests: cleanup leftover mounts
commit.message:
LU-20619 tests: cleanup leftover mounts

When a test fails and doesn't unmount what it just mounted, that
could lead to a busy error when we try to unconfigure lnet in
reinit_dlc. This patch ensures we don't have mounted targets by
calling "cleanupall -f".

To make that check meaningful, stopall() now accumulates the status
of unmountmds/unmountoss/unmountmgs (which in turn keep the return
code of "stop <facet> -f") and returns it instead of always
returning 0. cleanupall() then propagates a non-zero status from
stopall and unload_modules instead of returning cleanup_gss's
status, so that callers using "cleanupall || error" actually detect
a failed recovery (e.g. a leftover mount or a still-busy lnet
reference) rather than continuing on stale state.

Test-Parameters: trivial testlist=sanity-lnet
Signed-off-by: Cyril Bordage <cbordage@whamcloud.com>
Change-Id: I4d90878e91abf05d882cd82c87b9b2585bbd91df
